name: MOTT'S SUPPOSED SITE
materialIdentity: The most famous forty feet in the territory, dug to bedrock by twelve years of certainty: a bowl of overlapping pits, a windlass, spoil heaps like hills; night (errata 98, 99 F)
note: Room 30, doc 20: Mott's supposed strike site -- the fake one (doc 01) -- in the diggings below the road to the claims (errata 99 A, F).

LOOK_AT.say: Coins, pressed into the dirt at the center. Men have been leaving money here.
repeat: Pennies, mostly. A dime. A brass button. A gold tooth, which I regard as a serious commitment.
Nobody takes them. In a town that would pick a nail out of the road, nobody takes them.
then: I don't know what for, and I don't think they do.

repeat: A coin settling as the dirt dries around it.
Nothing. Whatever they paid for has not been delivered.

LOOK_AT.say: The original stake from Mott's filing, or the fourth replica of it — the first three were stolen by admirers. The town cannot agree which this is, and guards it either way.
repeat: It is painted, which no survey stake is. Admirers paint it every spring.
A small brass plaque at its foot reads ORIGINAL. The plaque has been replaced twice.

LISTEN_TO.say: It hums when the wind crosses the shaft. The site's one note, played on a lie.
repeat: The hum again, over the shaft: one note, a little sharp, held for as long as there is wind.
Nothing, in the lull. A lie at rest sounds exactly like the truth at rest.

overrides.PICK_UP: Whichever replica it is, taking it would make me the fourth thief of a fake of a lie. There are depths, and I have a claim in them already.

LOOK_AT.say: Carved into the one standing post: initials, dozens deep, overwritten into a texture.
repeat: Dates too. The oldest are eleven years old and the newest is this week. Proof, it turns out, needs constant renewal.
There is no room left to carve, and somebody has started on the back of the post.
then: Every man who ever proved the site empty signed the proof.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. The names have said their piece.
repeat: Nothing. Dozens of men, all done talking.
Wood ticking in the sun. The post is drying out, one name at a time.

overrides.USE: There is no room left to carve. The proof is fully subscribed.

LOOK_AT.say: A stone, with MOTT cut into it by somebody who cared. It is not a claim marker.
repeat: The letters are cut deep and straight. Whoever did it had time, a good chisel and no particular reason.
There are dried flowers at its foot. Somebody comes here to remember a man nobody can describe.
then: It is not anything. Somebody carved it because there was nothing here to look at.

repeat: Nothing. Stone, with a name in it, keeping it.
Wind across the letters, a faint whistle in the M.

LOOK_AT.say: A windlass over the deepest shaft, rope long gone.
repeat: The crank is worn to the shape of a hand. Several hands. The same shape.
The shaft below it is boarded over. Somebody fell in once, I am told, and found nothing there either.
then: It lowered a decade of hope down a hole and hauled up gravel.

LISTEN_TO.say: The frame moans in the wind. It has earned it.
repeat: A slow creak as the wind turns the drum half an inch and lets it go.
The moan again, longer. The frame and the wind have been at this for years.

LOOK_AT.say: Fresh. Somebody was here this week, and dug, in ground that has been dug four hundred times, and went home.
repeat: Neat work, square corners. He took care, digging in ground he must have known was empty.
The spoil is heaped on the side facing town, so nobody would see him from there.
Nothing. He has gone home.
Dirt crumbling at the edge. The ground is filling it back in, patiently, as it does.

LOOK_AT.say: From here the town is a smudge of chimney smoke and one bright steeple, keeping an eye on the place.
repeat: The road between is worn by pilgrims, going out hopeful and coming back the same, which is a kind of faith.
From the famous nothing, Consolation looks like something. It is the best view of it in the district.

LISTEN_TO.say: The bell, very thin, carried on the wind.
repeat: Hammering, small and far. Somebody is building something on top of all this.
Nothing for a moment, then the bell again, as though the town had remembered itself.

LOOK_AT.say: From the famous nothing, you can just see my worthless something — one ridge over, unregarded, mine. Nobody has ever dug there twice.
repeat: From here it looks exactly like every piece of ground in between, which is its own kind of camouflage.
I can see my marker from here if I squint, leaning the way it leans.

LISTEN_TO.say: Quiet, from that direction. It has never had anything to say. I find I like it for that.
repeat: Still quiet from over there. It is very good at it.
Nothing from that direction. It is the most restful thing I own.

LOOK_AT.say: Broken sieves and worn pans, discarded where the last hopeful stood.
repeat: A pan with its bottom worn clean through. Somebody swirled until there was nothing left to swirl with.
The meshes get finer toward the top of the pile. The hopes got smaller and so did the holes.
then: The tools give up before the men, but not by much.

LISTEN_TO.say: Mesh, buzzing faintly in the gusts. The pile still sifts the wind.
repeat: A rattle as a gust goes through: tin, wire and patience, all past use.
Nothing between gusts. The pile waits for the wind like everything else here.

LOOK_AT.say: Scraped clean as a plate. Men have gone over this stone with brushes. With brushes.
repeat: There are scratches in it from every tool the Mercantile has ever sold, in roughly the order it sold them.
It is the cleanest rock in the district and the least interesting. I've looked at it longer than it deserves, in honor of everyone else who did.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Stone that has answered the same question ten thousand times.
repeat: Nothing. It has had nothing to hide for twelve years, and has said so, under brushes.
Nothing. Brushed by ten thousand men, it has nothing left to confide.

overrides.USE: Ten thousand men, with brushes. There is nothing left to do to this stone except apologize.

LOOK_AT.say: Spoil heaps, grown into small hills of their own.
repeat: Grass has started on the oldest heap. Even nature has stopped waiting for a result.
Somebody has sifted the heaps too, and heaped the siftings. It is heaps all the way down.
then: The site has produced a new landscape and no gold.

LISTEN_TO.say: Gravel trickling down a slope: a small, dry, continual surrender.
repeat: A scrabble on the warm side. A lizard, probably, minding the property.
Nothing. Dirt that has been looked through has nothing left to say.

LOOK_AT.say: The famous nothing, resting. The pilgrims have stopped coming — the gold has an address now, and it was never this one. The moon can have its claim back.
The most famous forty feet in the territory, excavated to bedrock and below by twelve years of certainty. It looks like the moon, if the moon had been disappointed in.
repeat: Turned over so many times that it is no longer ground so much as an opinion about where ground used to be.
There is a bench at the edge for pilgrims. It faces the diggings the way pews face an altar.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind in the workings, same as ever. It sounds different when it is no longer lying to anyone.
Wind in the workings. A hollow instrument, played badly.
repeat: Nothing. Nothing whatsoever. It's the emptiest sound I've heard since I arrived.
The wind, and under it, faint and far off, somebody's pick. Even here, somebody is still checking.

overrides.TALK_TO: 'You could have been anywhere,' I told the famous nothing. The wind moved a sieve. I chose to hear an apology; nothing here corrects you.

LOOK_AT.say: Perhaps four hundred separate diggings, overlapping. Ten thousand men have come here, individually, each certain that the others had looked in the wrong place.
repeat: They overlap so completely that nobody can say where one man's hope ended and the next began.
One pit still has a ladder in it. The man who climbed out did not come back for it.
Loose dirt sliding back into a pit, slowly refilling what was emptied.
Nothing. Four hundred holes, every one keeping the same secret, which is that there isn't one.

exits.name: THE ROAD

LOOK_AT.say: The way back to the road. Behind me, the most dug-over ground in the territory. Ahead, a road nobody has ever bothered to dig.
repeat: Pans left at the edge, where men set them down for the walk back and never picked them up again.
Every man who has walked out this way was sure of something on the way in.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind across all those holes behind me. It sounds like a church organ that has given up.
repeat: The road, out of sight, and empty.
A pan shifting on the stones as the night cools it.
